about: Optional plugins and MCP servers that /flow-setup extensions can offer. Checked on 2026-11-16 against the Claude Code plugin catalog. Commands change: /flow-setup re-checks each one (claude plugin details, the source repository) before installing. Nothing here is installed without the dev's ok.

extensions.author: Microsoft
extensions.signal: a web frontend or an HTTP UI in the repository
extensions.why: Drives a real browser: end-to-end tests, screenshots, checking a UI change actually renders.

extensions.author: Upstash
extensions.signal: third-party libraries or frameworks whose APIs change between versions
extensions.why: Fetches version-specific library documentation, so the executor does not code against an API from memory.

extensions.author: GitHub
extensions.signal: tasks in GitHub Issues, or reviews on GitHub pull requests
extensions.why: Lets agents read issues and pull requests. The gh CLI is an alternative with no install.

extensions.author: GitLab
extensions.signal: tasks in GitLab Issues, or merge requests on GitLab
extensions.why: Lets agents read issues and merge requests. The glab CLI is an alternative with no install.

extensions.author: Linear
extensions.why: Lets agents read Linear issues and their acceptance criteria.

extensions.author: Atlassian
extensions.signal: tasks in Jira, or product documentation in Confluence
extensions.why: Lets agents read Jira issues and Confluence pages. Each dev authorizes with their own Atlassian login.
claude: claude mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp --scope project

extensions.author: Anthropic
extensions.signal: any repository handling user data, credentials or external input
extensions.why: Warns on risky patterns while code is being written, before the security lens sees it.

extensions.author: Anthropic
extensions.why: Review agents for error handling, test coverage, comments and type design. Useful on a PR that did not go through the flow.

extensions.author: Anthropic
extensions.signal: the repository's main language: typescript-lsp, pyright-lsp, gopls-lsp, rust-analyzer-lsp, jdtls-lsp, kotlin-lsp, csharp-lsp, ruby-lsp, php-lsp, swift-lsp, clangd-lsp, lua-lsp
extensions.why: Go-to-definition and diagnostics from a language server instead of text search.

extensions.author: Anthropic
extensions.why: Design guidance for interfaces the executor builds.

extensions.author: Matt Pocock
extensions.trust: community, listed in the official marketplace
extensions.signal: the team wants a harder interview before code
extensions.why: Includes grill-me and grilling (relentless questioning of a plan), tdd, to-spec, diagnosing-bugs and domain-modeling.
extensions.overlaps: Its spec and ticket skills overlap the refiner. Use grill-me inside the triage, and keep the contract in 01-contract.md.

extensions.author: Jesse Vincent
extensions.trust: community, listed in the official marketplace
extensions.signal: the team wants red/green TDD and systematic debugging habits
extensions.why: Skills for TDD, systematic debugging and brainstorming.
extensions.overlaps: It has its own subagent-driven development flow. Running both makes two orchestrators compete: use its TDD and debugging skills, not its flow.

extensions.author: DietrichGebert
extensions.signal: the codebase tends to grow abstractions nobody asked for
extensions.why: Pushes the executor to the smallest change that works. ponytail-review adds an over-engineering pass to the review.
claude: claude plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail --scope project

extensions.author: thedotmack
extensions.signal: a dev wants automatic memory across their own sessions
extensions.why: Captures observations from sessions and injects relevant ones at the start of the next.
extensions.overlaps: It is personal and automatic. LEARNINGS.md is shared, reviewed and tagged. Keep team rules in LEARNINGS.md. It records session content locally, so check it against your sensitive-data rules first. Recommend user scope, not project.
